comment: Pairs not worth attempting again without new information. A null solver blocks the problem for every integration, which is right when the limit is in the reference itself. generation.coverage drops these from the work queue; add an entry when you block a pair, with the evidence that justifies it.

blockers.detail: The reference's own model is unsolved at both 60s and 180s on json:1, with the candidate never running. Solver-independent, so no integration can get past the second instance. Recorded second-hand from an earlier cpmpy_python run whose artifacts were not retained; the pair_deferred event in the cited ledger is the surviving record. Re-prove it before lifting this blocker.
Only the embedded example of 7 distinct instances is reachable; the reference exceeds 60s on json:2 with the candidate never running. One instance is too little to retain.

Z3 could not prove the minimum ruler length for any of the three instances at 180s. A performance limit of this solver on this problem, not a reference or contract fault, so it is blocked for z3_python only. A materially better encoding would justify retrying.

The instance field Qualified is a ragged array: one variable-length list of qualified workers per task. MiniZinc's data interface binds a list of lists as a rectangular 2D array, so the runner fails with 'non-uniform array literal' before solving, whatever the model says. Reshaping the field inside run.py would be the problem-specific converter the integration's skill rules out, so this is an integration limit rather than a modelling one.
